questions.question: What type of reproduction is typically carried out by flowering plants?
options: Asexual reproduction only
Sexual reproduction
Binary fission
Budding

questions.question: Why is plant reproduction vital for all animal life on Earth?
options: Plants consume carbon dioxide and directly heat the planet.
Plants are producers that form the base of food chains and provide food.
Plants release minerals into the atmosphere for animals to breathe.
Plants actively clean water sources through pollination.

questions.question: What are the female gametes in flowering plants called?
options: Pollen grains
Anthers
Egg cells (ova)
Stigmas

questions.question: Which structures in flowering plants carry the male gametes?
options: Pollen grains
Ovules
Petals
Sepals

questions.question: Where are seeds formed in a flowering plant?
options: In the anther
In the pollen tube
In the ovary
On the petals

questions.question: Botanically speaking, what is a fruit?
options: A mature and ripened ovary of a seed-producing plant
A modified leaf used for attracting animal pollinators
The swollen tip of a stem that stores water
An enlarged pollen grain containing multiple embryos

questions.question: What are the three primary agents that seeds are adapted to be dispersed by?
options: Animals, wind, and water
Insects, soil, and sunlight
Gravity, temperature, and rocks
Fungi, fire, and oxygen

questions.question: What is the main role of a pollinator in plant sexual reproduction?
options: To digest the seeds and spread them in their droppings
To transfer pollen from one flower to another
To absorb nutrients from the soil for the roots
To protect the flower buds from wind damage

questions.question: What does the term "food security" mean?
options: Locking up food supplies in secure vaults to prevent theft
Having enough affordable and nutritious food in an area or country
Controlling the DNA of crops to make them pest-resistant
Ensuring food is packaged in sterile, airtight containers

questions.question: What is the definition of pollination?
options: The fusion of male and female gamete nuclei
The transfer of pollen from the male anther to the female stigma
The growth of a seed into a young seedling
The release of seeds from a ripened fruit

questions.question: Which type of pollination increases genetic variation within a plant species?
options: Self-pollination
Cross-pollination
Wind pollination only
Insect pollination only

questions.question: What is fertilisation in plants?
options: The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
The dispersal of seeds away from the parent plant
The fusion of the nuclei from the male and female gametes
The absorption of nutrients from the soil by roots

questions.question: In a plant growth investigation, when should you use a line graph instead of a bar chart to display data?
options: When the independent variable is categoric
When the independent variable is continuous
When you have fewer than five total measurements
When the dependent variable is qualitative

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of seed that will successfully germinate on moist cotton wool under the right conditions?
options: Cress seeds
Oak acorns
Coconut seeds
Pine nuts

questions.question: Why must control variables be kept the same during an investigation into seed germination?
options: To ensure the independent variable can be easily changed
To ensure the results are recorded in a bar chart
To ensure a valid conclusion can be drawn
To make the seeds germinate as quickly as possible

questions.question: What is the main reason for repeating measurements for each value in a seed dispersal investigation?
options: To change the independent variable halfway through
To identify anomalous results and calculate a mean
To ensure that the seed template does not get damaged
To prove that the hypothesis is always correct
